a1.label: 1. The phishing email pretended to be from...
a1.why: The text says the email appeared to come from the IT department.

a2.label: 2. The link led to...
a2.why: The text says the link led to a fake login page copying the company design.

a3.label: 3. Attackers couldn't access accounts because of...
a3.why: The text says two-factor authentication stopped the attackers.

a4.label: 4. How many colleagues entered credentials?
a4.why: The text says three colleagues entered their credentials.

a5.label: 5. If you get a suspicious message, you should...
a5.why: The text says to forward the message to the security team.

a6.label: 6. According to the text, the IT department...
a6.why: The text says IT never asks for credentials by email.

b1.label: 1. Fake emails tricking users into revealing passwords
b1.why: ‘Phishing’ is fake emails that trick users into revealing passwords.

b2.label: 2. Protects data by making it unreadable
b2.why: ‘Encryption’ protects data by making it unreadable without a key.

b3.label: 3. A software update that fixes a security hole
b3.why: A ‘patch’ is a software update that fixes a security hole.

b4.label: 4. Password plus a code from your phone
b4.why: ‘Two-factor authentication’ requires a password plus a code from your phone.

b5.label: 5. Connect securely to the network from home
b5.why: A ‘VPN’ lets employees connect securely to the company network remotely.

b6.label: 6. A weakness attackers can exploit
b6.why: A ‘vulnerability’ is a weakness that attackers can exploit.

b7.label: 7. Viruses, worms and ransomware
b7.why: Viruses, worms and ransomware are all types of malware.

c1.label: 1. If you ___ a phishing link...
c1.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’.

c2.label: 2. If the firewall is misconfigured, traffic ___ blocked
c2.why: The Type I result clause uses ‘will’ + passive.

c4.label: 4. If an update ___ available...
c4.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’.

c5.label: 5. Employees ___ use a VPN on public Wi-Fi

c6.label: 6. If we ___ install the patch...
c6.why: The logic requires the negative: not installing the patch leaves the vulnerability exploitable.

c7.label: 7. Unless you verify the sender, you ___ open it
c7.why: ‘Unless’ (= if not) pairs with advice against an action: ‘shouldn't’.
